pairs.evidence: app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:31 Every meter in the closed vocabulary is a flow: one act per debit, added into a window-closed per-period counter. That is one of the two kinds the subject says a plain sum gets right. A search of app/_lib and app/_lib/billing for highWater, high_water, timeWeighted and integral found nothing, and there is no seat or held-level meter.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:31 No meter is something the customer holds. All five describe acts (posted, hired, analysed, designed, interviewed), so the value between events is zero.

app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:287 Each debit source is a chargeable act, not an add/remove change of state, which is the technique's own 'when not to use'. Org seats exist (org-service.ts) but are not billed.

app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:317 Prepaid credits are consumed at event time, but the debit refuses non-positive quantities and refundMeterUsage was removed. The aggregate is monotonic by construction, so the decision rule 'skip the mark' applies.

app/_lib/billing/entitlements.ts:222 Window-closed: the allowance read is the counter for this period key alone. The only carry is the one-time calendar-to-anchored re-key (ADR 0023), not a recurring level seed.

pairs.subject: usage-aggregation-semantics

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/db/billing.ts:385 A flow counter summed per period key. There is no level whose between-event value is nonzero.
app/_lib/db/llm.ts:554 Counts are event counts (calls), not distinct-identifier holdings, so there is no add/remove vocabulary to replay.
app/_lib/db/billing.ts:376 The balance is a ledger of the effects actually issued (grants, consumes, refunds), not a peak ratchet. There is no decreasing level to ratchet over.
app/_lib/db/billing.ts:408 calendarUsageCarried is a half-open, window-bounded carry for a period re-key migration, read from the journal. No metric spans periods, so there is no recurring seed.
